text.p: Italian debt markets and the lira reined in their earlier enthusiasm to stand around 50 basis points higher on the day, instead of up at the record 120.98 peak set on the December LIFFE future.

Players were now waiting to hear about the government's 1997 budget package, due to be unveiled Friday. Traders stressed that despite optimism of investors piling into Italy from all angles, the budget process still had potential for hitches and support from the hard left for the package was not a forgone conclusion.
"There's so much good news priced in - any squabbles over the budget and the market's set itself up for one almighty fall," said Jonathan York at Cater Allen Futures in London.
The February 2006 Btp was 48 basis points up at the close at 105.80, with the spread over the 10-year benchmark Bund drawing in to below 270 before settling back at that level later.
The December future was 59 basis points higher at 120.54 with the next target the 121 area. But traders were sceptical as to how aggressively the market could climb now.

The future has rallied acutely in the last three days from just above 118.00 on Wednesday. The lira has also rocketed, powering through the psychological 1,000 per mark level late last night to the dizzy heights of 995.25, the strongest level since August 1994. It was at 1,000.50/0.80 by 1540 GMT.

Analysts said the 1,000 level was now "porous" meaning the lira could cross the line with ease. Speculation circulated the Bank of Italy was buying marks to stem its rise but traders were unable to confirm the talk.

Later, once the cash market had closed, trade minister Augusto Fantozzi said the total budget package would be for 50 trillion lire of measures, including a "euro tax" and savings on health and pensions.
Futures immediately climbed to 120.80, not far from the record peak. --Milan bureau +392 66129507
